clue.text: It takes months to boil off

parts.note: December is shortened to DEC
October is shortened to OCT

explanation.surface: A slow cooking process takes months to boil something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes months' describes the answer, built from two months' abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Decocting means extracting a substance's essence by boiling it down, a verb for boiling away.

clue.text: Some say stain leather in compound

indicators.note: some people saying it signals that the words are to be heard, not read

parts.note: a stain is a DYE, and leather is OX HIDE

explanation.surface: Some people say you should stain leather using a chemical compound.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, DYE + OX HIDE runs together as the name of a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A dioxide is a chemical compound with two oxygen atoms per molecule, carbon dioxide being the best known.

clue.text: Reserved costlier mounts for fur supplier

parts.note: a coy person is shy or reserved

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: prices that are up are costlier

explanation.surface: A shy, pricier item climbs on show at a furrier's.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a South American rodent farmed for its fur, sold as nutria.

clue.text: See 24
Shuffle, say, round well to find creeper

indicators.note: the music player's name goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the iPod Shuffle is one model of iPod, so it is an example of one
'well' and 'so' are both sentence-openers in speech

explanation.surface: A card trick: shuffle the deck, go round the well, and find the climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' looks like an anagram signal but is a brand name, the iPod Shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a crustacean such as the woodlouse, a small crawling creature, so a creeper.

clue.text: Bloodhound, I think, ignored trash

indicators.note: the hesitation is ignored, so it is left out of the detective's name

parts.note: a bloodhound is slang for a detective, here Sherlock Holmes
a hesitant 'er' is said while thinking

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a bloodhound as worthless rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shlock is a Yiddish-derived word for cheap, shoddy goods, trash in the sense of junk.

clue.text: Old shabby togs the best clothes for bouncer

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the choice wraps round the other letters

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best

indicators.note: shabby clothes are worn out of shape, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Old shabby clothes compared with the best outfit worn by a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but it is a toy you jump on; 'shabby' reorders the clothes word and 'clothes' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogo stick is a spring-loaded toy you bounce on, so it is literally a bouncer.

clue.text: Runs I'd built up in scramble

indicators.note: in a down clue, building up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: trots are short runs
I'd contracted is I-D

explanation.surface: Someone builds up runs in a frantic scramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built up' turns TROTS + ID backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort or to scramble a signal are both to garble it beyond recognition.

clue.text: The house opposite has decorators busy

indicators.note: busy workers move things about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Neighbours notice decorators at work in the house over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges HAS and DECORATORS; the definition describes where the house opposite stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A house opposite yours is located on the far side of the street from you.

clue.text: Spotted old Whig close to Tory

parts.note: Charles James Fox was a famous eighteenth-century Whig politician

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A historical Whig politician was seen near a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: Whigs and Tories were Britain's two old parties; 'Spotted' looks like 'seen' but means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxed or foxy paper is stained with brownish spots, so spotted with age.

clue.text: Doctor saw one overhead, circling

indicators.note: the overhead cost circles, enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: oncost is a British term for an overhead expense
to log is to saw up timber
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor saw something circling overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts LOGI inside ONCOST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncologist is a cancer specialist, a type of medical doctor.

clue.text: Muddles ahead in M6 shambles

indicators.note: the lead sits in the middle of the jumbled motorway
a shambles is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the M6 is a British motorway; read M and SIX
a team that is one up is ahead

explanation.surface: Confusion ahead on a chaotic stretch of the M6 motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' turns M and SIX into MIXS; 'in' places UP inside. The M6 is a major British motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mix-ups are confusions or blunders, the same as muddles.

clue.text: Firm recalled watchmaker at noon for special event

indicators.note: called back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
Casio is a Japanese watch brand

explanation.surface: A firm recalls watches at midday for a big event.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a notable happening or celebration, so a special event.

clue.text: What bailiffs do with bias? Scratch head

indicators.note: scratching the head means deleting the first letter

parts.note: to prepossess is to prejudice, to bias in advance

explanation.surface: A puzzled person asks how bailiffs work with prejudice and scratches their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch head' looks like puzzlement but removes the first letter of PREPOSSESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailiffs seize goods or property back from defaulting debtors, which is to repossess them.

clue.text: Uneasy with this hormone, rep produces progesterone

indicators.note: an uneasy combination is unsettled, so its letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A sales rep is worried that one hormone produces another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uneasy' combines the answer with REP to make the letters of PROGESTERONE; remove REP and the rest spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen (estrogen in US spelling) is the main female sex hormone.

clue.text: Dazzling display in Port Talbot at the front

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dazzling show is staged at the front in Port Talbot.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Talbot is a Welsh steel town; 'Port' alone is RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot of colour is a vivid, dazzling display.

clue.text: Smell ship's captain

parts.note: BO is short for body odour, a smell
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone smells the ship's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person in charge, as a captain is of a ship or team.

clue.text: Using agent before enlisting expert in axes

parts.note: 'by' can mean before, as in by noon
a pro is an expert
x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: An agent goes ahead in recruiting an expert in axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by proxy means getting someone else to act for you, through an agent.

clue.text: Native Americans caught lion — hunt's over

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lion is a celebrated person or hero, as in lionised

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to hunt is to seek

explanation.surface: Native hunters catch a lion and the hunt is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SEEK into KEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Royal duke visits car maker in part of Wales

parts.note: R is short for royal, as in RN

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the letter enters the maker's name

parts.note: Honda is a Japanese car maker

explanation.surface: A royal duke tours a car factory in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhondda is a valley in South Wales, once a coal-mining area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley and district in South Wales.

clue.text: Demanding dope during leave

indicators.note: one thing during another sits inside it

parts.note: to exit is to leave
dope and gen are slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone asks for drugs while on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent describes something pressing or requiring much, so demanding.

clue.text: This pot some occasionally steal

indicators.note: taking only some letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally pinches this pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steal' looks like theft but means creep quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal or tiptoe is to move silently and stealthily.

clue.text: I fill small beer with more punch

indicators.note: the letter fills the gap, going inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Someone fills a small glass of strong beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportier means livelier and more powerful, as a sportier car has more punch.

clue.text: Ring teams to corral a large sorrel

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

indicators.note: to corral is to pen in, so the teams enclose the other letters

parts.note: an XI is a team of eleven, so XIS are teams

explanation.surface: Ring the teams to round up a big chestnut horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorrel' looks like a horse colour but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxalis is the genus of wood sorrel, a plant with sour clover-like leaves.

clue.text: Sailor abandons mollusc for sole

indicators.note: the sailor leaves, so those letters go

parts.note: the abalone is an edible mollusc
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor gives up eating shellfish for a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like fish but means only.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone and sole both mean single, without anyone else.

clue.text: In today's game make a big hash to start

definitions.text: In today's game make a big hash to start

parts.words: In today's game make a big hash to start
parts.note: the game begins with a grid drawn like a large hash sign, and today's puzzle is full of O and X letters

explanation.surface: A friend recommends a fresh start by making a big mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is played on a grid shaped like a hash sign; 'today's' points to the puzzle's many O and X letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The game of Xs and Os (tic-tac-toe in the US) starts by drawing a three-by-three grid.

clue.text: Steers by intercepting one mobile

indicators.note: the letter intercepts, cutting into the jumbled word
a mobile thing moves, so the letters move about

parts.note: X means by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Cattle are steered by someone who intercepts them on a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' turns ONE into OEN; 'intercepting' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers are castrated bulls raised for beef, so they are oxen.

clue.text: Yankee gets on with the German over there

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet
taken as written
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: An American gets along with a German over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word meaning at that distant place.

clue.text: Extremely easy-going officer accepts cuts

indicators.note: taking something in, so the officer holds the other letters

parts.note: Lt is short for lieutenant
to axe is to cut, so axes are cuts

explanation.surface: A relaxed officer accepts budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxest means most lenient or relaxed, the superlative of a word for easy-going.
